notes: Complete independent reading finished with no proposed textual, punctuation, notation, placement or state change. The supplied current page is retained exactly.

All 43 existing comparison loci, all 11 recorded decisions (including the 7 assigned C marks), all 6 unresolved places, all 4 settled certainty decisions and all 12 inventory elements were reviewed. Both-witness agreements were also checked directly in the native halves.

The six retained doubts are the canceled En-like opening, canceled revêtement-like word, aborted canceled p, the possible zero before x-prime in the stabilizer index, the canceled-Pi/reference-mark cluster below (51), and the live/deleted status of the final la-like word. Every doubt remains explicitly marked in the current text.
The only new first crop concerns i.e. It confirms the independently written internal and terminal points, so it causes no correction or certainty-only change. No decided place was recropped.

The source's literal half sign, universal quantifier, geometric joining dash, Ens/ss-groupes/ens/autom./mb abbreviations, braced component notation, barred-Sigma colon and final unpointed l’autom all remain as written.

The two-row map (50) has a plain right arrow in its first row and a barred-tail right arrow in its second. Map (51) has a plain right arrow and the label near its head. No additional diagram, drawing, underline or marginal prose was found.
Author page 16 is a top-center text element. The lighter thin archive folio 96 at lower left is another unnamed hand and remains a margin note; no macro-only comparison row is introduced.
The last short la-like word is not repaired to a grammatical phrase, and its cancellation remains uncertain. The leaf ends at nécessai-; no completion is supplied from outside the assigned page.

The supplied root event 142-097-R1 explains the stabilizer-map descent and the component/group distinction. It was read as existing apparatus, not independently re-proved in this audit. No new mathematical check event is claimed.
An unchanged proposed.tex is supplied because the assignment requested that file; it is a byte-for-byte copy of the packet's current consolidated.tex.
